existing.description: The Eric Bleumink Fellowship is a University of Groningen grant for nationals of a listed group of countries who hold provisional or unconditional admission to a one or two year master's programme starting in September. The grant covers tuition fee, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance. It is nomination-based: the University of Groningen's Admission Office decides which admitted applicants are nominated, so there is no direct scholarship application. The University of Groningen states that a considerable number of students apply each year while it can issue only a limited number of grants.
eligibility: Have received provisional or unconditional admission for a master programme before February; only then are applicants considered for a grant
Have excellent academic performance, preferably to be confirmed by letters of recommendation
Have excellent grades during their bachelor/undergraduate studies
Have excellent English language proficiency, in accordance with the admission requirements of the program of choice
Be available for the whole period of the programme and be able to take part in the entire programme
Be in good health, so that health insurance in the Netherlands can be arranged
Hold the nationality of a country appearing in Appendix 1
Have no other means of financing the study in question
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country in Appendix 1 of the fellowship, have received provisional or unconditional admission to a University of Groningen master's programme before February, have excellent academic performance and excellent undergraduate grades, have excellent English matching the chosen programme's admission requirements, be available for the whole programme, be in good health so Dutch health insurance can be arranged, and have no other means of financing the study.
existing.english_requirement: Excellent English language proficiency, in accordance with the admission requirements of the program of choice
application_method: Apply for admission to a University of Groningen master's programme through the normal admission route
No separate scholarship application: the Admission Office nominates admitted applicants
existing.selection_notes: The University of Groningen's Admission Office, in consultation with the Admission Boards of its faculties, determines which applicants are nominated. A considerable number of students apply each year while the University can issue only a limited number of grants.
existing.best_fit: Nationals of the Appendix 1 developing-country list who already hold or will secure an unconditional offer for a one or two year University of Groningen master's programme starting in September.
existing.notes: All master's programmes are eligible ("Programmes: All"). The grant is awarded only for programmes starting in September, so February or April start dates are not eligible.
existing.duration: 1 or 2 year master's degree programme, starting in September only
existing.application_period: Annual cycle tied to master's admission for a September start; master's applications to be completed before 1 December and admission offers received before February
existing.deadline_display: There is no scholarship application deadline: "It is not possible to actively apply for an Eric Bleumink Fellowship Scholarship. Suitable candidates will be informed about a nomination." Applicants must hold a provisional or unconditional admission offer for a master programme received before February, and their master's application "should be completed by the applicant before 1st of December".
existing.program_type: Master's scholarship grant awarded by the university, nomination-based
